authoredSolutions.27: Because of the inert pair effect, the \(+2\) state is the stable one for Pb while the \(+4\) state is the stable one for Sn. Reaction (1), \(PbO_{2} + Pb \rightarrow 2PbO\), converts Pb(IV) and Pb(0) into the more stable Pb(II), so it is spontaneous and \(\Delta_{r}G^{\circ}(1) < 0\). Reaction (2), \(SnO_{2} + Sn \rightarrow 2SnO\), converts the stable Sn(IV) into the less stable Sn(II), so it is non-spontaneous and \(\Delta_{r}G^{\circ}(2) > 0\) (indeed SnO disproportionates in the reverse sense). Hence \(\Delta_{r}G^{\circ}(1) < 0;\ \Delta_{r}G^{\circ}(2) > 0\).
authoredSolutions.28: The figure shows two identical M electrodes dipping into \(M^{+}\) solutions of concentrations \(c_{1}\) and \(c_{2}\) separated by a semi-permeable membrane, i.e. a concentration cell. authoredSolutions.29: A nucleotide is built from a heterocyclic base, a phosphate group and a pentose sugar. The bases (adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine, uracil) are flat, achiral heterocycles, and the phosphate linkage carries no stereocentre in the polymer backbone. The chirality therefore comes from the sugar: \(D\)-2-deoxyribose in DNA and \(D\)-ribose in RNA, both of which carry several stereocentres and occur naturally in the \(D\) form. Hence the \(D\)-sugar component.

In \(CH_{3}^{+}\) the three hydrogens are attached directly to the cationic carbon itself, not to an adjacent carbon; there is no alpha carbon at all, so the number of hyperconjugative structures is zero, not three. authoredSolutions.35: The substrate in the figure is a cyclopentane bearing Br on two adjacent carbons (C1, C2), an ethyl group on C5 and a methyl group on C3. (i) Zn with heat removes the vicinal dihalide to give the alkene, 3-methyl-5-ethylcyclopent-1-ene, with the double bond between C1 and C2. (ii) \(HBr\) adds through a carbocation. Both alkene carbons are equally substituted, so protonation gives a secondary cation which then undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to a tertiary cation. Two tertiary cations are possible: one at the methyl-bearing carbon and one at the ethyl-bearing carbon. Counting alpha hydrogens, the cation on the methyl-bearing carbon has \(3 + 2 + 2 = 7\) alpha C-H bonds while the one on the ethyl-bearing carbon has only \(2 + 2 + 2 = 6\). The more hyperconjugatively stabilised cation is therefore the methyl-substituted one, and \(Br^{-}\) captures it to give 1-bromo-1-methyl-3-ethylcyclopentane, which is option (B). Option (A) is the unrearranged adduct and option (C) is the product from the less stable tertiary cation.
